profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, traded on public markets under the ticker NVDA. Its website for the Nemotron product line describes the company as building multimodal foundation models and agentic AI infrastructure, with its most recent annual revenue reported in a 10-K filing covering the period ending January 25, 2026, at $215,938,000,000.

NVIDIA's primary AI offerings tracked on this site are the Nemotron model family and NIM microservices. The company describes Nemotron as a family of multimodal, open AI models designed for agentic reasoning across tasks including advanced math, graduate-level science, visual understanding, speech recognition, text-to-speech, neural machine translation, and retrieval-augmented generation. Specific models mentioned on the site include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, described as helping agents complete specialized tasks faster, and NeMo Switchyard, described as routing steps to the appropriate model. NVIDIA NIM is described as inference microservices that package Nemotron and other foundation models for secure, scalable enterprise deployment, available from build.nvidia.com and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for that deployment path. Bryan Catanzaro, identified as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site discussing the vision behind Nemotron. The site also names ServiceNow as a partner that evaluated Nemotron's visual question-and-answer accuracy.

The held facts indicate NVIDIA has a significant litigation footprint, with 175 cases associated with California exposure recorded in this site's database, though no specific case details are provided in the available data. The company holds an SEC CIK of 0001045810 and no MCP server presence is recorded.
